paragraph: Presidential Decree 272/24, published in the [Diário da República on 5 December 2024](<https://lex.ao/docs/presidente-da-republica/2024/decreto-presidencial-n-o-272-24-de-05-de-dezembro/>), approved Angola's ICT White Paper 2023-2027. The [White Paper](<https://livrobranco.gov.ao/site/pdf/LBTIC.pdf>) names the National Broadband Strategy and the National Broadband Network (RNBL) as its basis, and states universal access to broadband as its objective. The decree text holds no numeric coverage, speed or price target. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No budget line, universal service fund allocation or financed programme tied to the plan has been found for the last three years. Operating would need money committed to the plan in the past three years.

The International Telecommunication Union's report on the [Africa-BB-Maps national event of October 2025](<https://africabbmaps.itu.int/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Bdi-Rapport_Evenement-National-Africa-BB-Maps_28-30-Octobre-2025.pdf>) lists the Stratégie Large Bande 2025, Burundi's broadband strategy, in the country's legal and regulatory framework. The report gives no period dates for the strategy and states no broadband targets. It names the regulator ARCT and the ICT secretariat SETIC as lead bodies. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No budget line, universal service fund allocation or financed programme tied to the plan has been found for the last three years. Operating would need money committed to the plan in the past three years.

The government's [project sheet](<https://beninrevele.bj/projet/119/deploiement-internet-haut-tres-haut-debit-ensemble-territoire-national-phase-/>) lists the high and very high speed internet deployment (phase 2) as a government project with status En cours. Its execution period is 2022 to 2026. [Agence Ecofin](<https://www.agenceecofin.com/actualites-numerique/2511-123743-haut-debit-le-benin-veut-generaliser-l-acces-d-ici-2025>) reported in November 2024 that the broadband project was costed at about 207 billion FCFA. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No budget line or fund allocation tied to the plan has been found. Operating would need money committed to the plan.

[Sidwaya reported the minister saying on 24 October 2025](<https://www.sidwaya.info/ministere-en-charge-de-la-transition-digitale-lobservatoire-de-lamenagement-numerique-lance/>) that Burkina Faso adopted its Schéma directeur d'aménagement numérique (SDAN) in 2019. Neither that report nor Wearetech states a period for the 2019 document. In the last twelve months, [ministry and territorial-development representatives met on 6 to 12 September 2026](<https://www.wearetech.africa/fr/fils/actualites/telecom/le-burkina-faso-repense-l-amenagement-numerique-de-son-territoire-a-l-horizon-2030>) to consolidate a draft revised SDAN running to 2030. No adopted successor has been found. No budget line, universal service fund allocation or financed programme tied to the plan has been found for the last three years. Operating would need money committed to the plan in the past three years.

The Ministry of Transport and Communications issued the [National Broadband Strategy, in its final version of June 2018](<https://www.bocra.org.bw/sites/default/files/documents/National-Broadband-Strategy-FINAL%28June2018%29.pdf>). It gives the Information Age Council the task of guiding implementation and monitoring progress. It sets two coverage targets: 2 Mbps for 50% of citizens by the end of 2014, and 20 Mbps for 90% of the population by 2018. No later plan or revision has been found, and no change in the last twelve months. No progress figure, budget line, universal service fund allocation or financed programme tied to the plan has been found. Operating would need money committed to the plan in the past three years.

The government's [press release of 4 September 2025](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/la-republique-centrafricaine-lance-un-ambitieux-programme-pour-lavenir-302546890.html) launches a USD 12.8bn investment programme built on its National Development Plan 2024-2028. Broadband is one part of that larger plan. The release sets a national target of 3,000 km of fibre-optic deployment by 2028 and reports no result delivered at its date. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No budget line, universal service fund allocation or financed programme tied to the plan has been found for the last three years. Operating would need money committed to the plan in the past three years.

The entry names no plan and gives no title, adoption date, period or broadband targets. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No budget line, universal service fund allocation or financed programme tied to the plan has been found for the last three years. Operating would need money committed to the plan in the past three years: a budget line, a universal service fund allocation or a financed programme tied to it.

The Universal Service Development Fund (FDSU) [unveiled a National Connectivity Strategy 2026-2035](<https://developingtelecoms.com/telecom-business/telecom-regulation/20678-drc-unveils-10-year-strategy-to-close-connectivity-gaps-through-shared-infrastructure.html>) in August 2026. It sets a 2030 target of 3,000 localities and 16 million people, with further consultations planned. The strategy dates from the last twelve months. Developing Telecoms reported on 13 August 2026 that the FDSU signed subsidy agreements with Airtel, Orange, Vodacom and Africell covering 40 localities and about 258,000 people. No source has been found that says the government has adopted the strategy. Establishing would need a national broadband plan adopted by the government or the minister, with its period not ended.

Cabo Verde's government [presented its proposed National Strategy for the Implementation of 5G on 10 September 2025](<https://www.governo.cv/cabo-verde-apresenta-estrategia-nacional-para-o-5g-e-ambiciona-ser-hub-digital-regional-ate-2030/>), with a goal of 90% internet penetration by 2026 and regional digital hub status by 2030. In the last twelve months, [Resolution No. 33/2026 of 20 February 2026 formally approved the strategy](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/02/16/cape-verde-launches-national-5g-strategy-to-accelerate-digital-nation-vision/>), according to that report. The report gives no plan period. No budget line, universal service fund allocation or financed programme tied to the plan has been found for the last three years. Operating would need money committed to the plan in the past three years.

The Ministry of Communication [launched Djibouti's Stratégie Nationale du Haut-Débit (SNHD) on 16 October 2024](<https://www.wearetech.africa/en/fils-uk/news/telecom/djibouti-unveils-plan-to-boost-internet-connectivity-and-affordability>). It is part of the Djibouti Digital Foundation project, which the World Bank supports. Early results reported at the launch were 250 km of fibre laid in the north and more than 100 administrative buildings connected. The [La Nation editorial](<https://www.lanation.dj/editorial-linclusion-numerique-comme-nouvel-horizon-par-ibrahim-miyir-ali/>) says the SNHD sets two scenarios for 2027, connecting ten cities or seven. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No government figures against the plan's own targets have been found, and its period is not stated. Mature would need the government to publish figures against the plan's own targets in the past three years.

The Ministry of Post and Telecommunications calls its plan the [Tout Fibre strategy](<https://www.echoroukonline.com/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AC%D8%B2%D8%A7%D8%A6%D8%B1-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A3%D9%88%D9%84%D9%89-%D8%A5%D9%81%D8%B1%D9%8A%D9%82%D9%8A%D8%A7-%D9%81%D9%8A-%D9%85%D8%AC%D8%A7%D9%84-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B1%D8%A8%D8%B7-%D8%A8>), which aims to generalise fibre by 2027 at the latest. The ministry's [page of 9 July 2025](<https://www.mpt.gov.dz/genaralization-of-access-to-fixed-internet/>) sets a goal of 7 million households on fixed internet by the end of 2027. It reports 6.6 million fixed subscribers in the first half of 2025. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed: a [ministry communique of 30 September 2026](<https://lasentinelle.dz/index.php/2026/10/01/gigacity-2026-alger-premiere-ville-africaine-du-tres-haut-debit/>) says the strategy aims to bring fibre to the whole territory by 2027. No budget line, universal service fund allocation or financed programme tied to the plan has been found for the last three years. Operating would need money committed to the plan.

The Ministry of Communications and Information Technology, through the NTRA, launched the [eMisr National Broadband Plan on 17 November 2011](<https://mcit.gov.eg/en/Media_Center/Latest_News/News/2367>). It was a two-phase plan. The first phase was a Framework for Broadband Development, and the second a Broadband Action Plan due in the second quarter of 2012. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No budget line, universal service fund allocation or financed programme tied to the plan has been found for the last three years, and no figures against its targets. Operating would need money committed to the plan in the past three years.

No stage is set. The only source found for Eritrea is a 2019 listing of countries with no national broadband plan, and it is too old to count. No plan or draft has been found, and no source dated in the last three years says the country has neither. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Absent would need a source from the past three years saying the country has no national broadband plan and none is being written.

In 2024 the government told [ITU's ICT Regulatory Tracker](<https://app.gen5.digital/tracker/metrics>) that Ethiopia has a national plan that involves broadband. The answer was self-reported. The entry names no plan and gives no title, adoption date, period or broadband targets. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No budget line, universal service fund allocation or financed programme tied to the plan has been found for the last three years. Operating would need money committed to the plan in the past three years: a budget line, a universal service fund allocation or a financed programme tied to it.

On 4 July 2016 the digital economy ministry announced that it wants a [national broadband promotion strategy and a costed operational plan](<https://www.digitalbusiness.africa/internet-le-gabon-veut-se-doter-dune-strategie-nationale-de-promotion-du-haut-debit/>) in the coming months. It had launched a broadband study to prepare both, and no strategy had yet been adopted. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source has been found that says a national broadband plan is adopted and still running, and nothing shows money committed to one. Establishing would need a national broadband plan adopted by the government or the minister, with its period not ended.

The Ministry of Communications issued the [National Broadband Policy and Implementation Strategy as Final Version 1.0 in October 2012](<https://nca.org.gh/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/National-Broadband-Policy-and-Implementation-Strategy.pdf>). Its targets were 40% household and 40% national broadband penetration by 2015. The target for 2020 was 90%. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No budget line or fund allocation tied to the plan has been found. No figures against its targets have been found. Operating would need money committed to the plan.

The Ministry of Information and Communication Infrastructure issued the [National Broadband Policy 2020-2024](<https://policies.gov.gm/d/caa6d521-5bad-11ec-9b31-029254d29bb1>) in June 2020 for a five-year period ending in 2024. The same month it commissioned the [National Broadband Strategy 2020-2024](<https://mocde.gov.gm/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/BROADBAND-STRATEGY-2024.pdf>), which sets a target of broadband coverage to more than 90% of the population by 2024. Neither document names a successor plan. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source has been found that says a national broadband plan is adopted and still running. Establishing would need a national broadband plan adopted by the government or the minister, with its period not ended.

Guinea-Bissau's [Strategic Plan of the Access and Universal Service Fund (FASU) for 2026-2031](<https://wardip.gw/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/Plano-Estrategico-do-UASF.pdf>) is a consultancy final report for the regulator ARN, dated 24 November 2025. It says it is still to be validated in a public stakeholder consultation, so it is a draft. It sets coverage targets before 2031: 99% of the population for 2G, 98% for 3G and 96% for 4G. [ITU's 2019 table of broadband plans](<http://broadband.itu.int/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/ITU_BroadbandPlans_2019.pdf>) recorded no national broadband policy. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a national broadband plan adopted by the government or the minister, with its period not ended.

On [11 December 2025](<https://www.guineaecuatorialpress.com/noticias/propuesta_de_colaboracion_con_el_banco_mundial_para_la_transformacion_digital>) the Ministry of Transport and Telecommunications presented to the World Bank a proposal for the Plan Nacional de Telecomunicaciones para la Transformación Digital. The plan includes a competitive network ensuring 100% coverage before 2030. The press article describes it as still to be designed, with World Bank technical assistance. The proposal dates from the last twelve months, and no earlier plan has been found. No source has been found that says a national broadband plan is adopted and still running, and nothing shows money committed to one. Establishing would need a national broadband plan adopted by the government or the minister, with its period not ended.

In November 2022 [President Ruto announced the Digital Superhighway's 100,000km national fibre target](<https://nation.africa/kenya/business/ruto-s-100-000km-fibre-optic-network-plan-falters-5580286>), which aims at broadband for the whole country by 2027. [The Digital Superhighway is funded through the Universal Service Fund](<https://nation.africa/kenya/business/ruto-s-100-000km-fibre-optic-network-plan-falters-5580286>). [The FY2026/27 budget gives Sh1.3 billion to maintain the national fibre backbone](<https://www.businessdailyafrica.com/bd/economy/ict-allocation-drops-to-sh8-6-billion-in-budget-5493262>). In the last twelve months, [Techweez reported in October 2026](<https://techweez.com/2026/10/27/kenya-fiber-optic-network-expansion/>) that the National Broadband Strategy 2025-2030 sets the same 100,000km target, against 40,000km of fibre today. No review or report from the last three years giving figures against the plan's own targets has been found. Mature would need the government to publish such figures.

In 2024 the government told [ITU's ICT Regulatory Tracker](<https://app.gen5.digital/tracker/metrics>) that Liberia has a national plan that involves broadband. The answer was self-reported. The entry names no plan and gives no title, adoption date, period or broadband targets. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No budget line, universal service fund allocation or financed programme tied to the plan has been found for the last three years. Operating would need money committed to the plan in the past three years: a budget line, a universal service fund allocation or a financed programme tied to it.

In the last twelve months Lesotho's Minister of Information, Communications, Science, Technology and Innovation [signed the Broadband Infrastructure Sharing Policy on 11 June 2026](<https://lestimes.com/?p=90715>), according to Lesotho Times. No plan period is given. Before that, the ministry held a [second draft of a Broadband and Shared Infrastructure Policy and Implementation Plan](<https://www.gov.ls/download/draft-broadband-and-shared-infrastructure-policy_1-0/>), dated 17 February 2025. No budget, fund allocation or delivery report has been found. No financed programme tied to the plan has been found for the last three years. Operating would need money committed to the plan.

Morocco's Plan National du Haut Débit (PNHD) is in its second phase. The ministry says it was [launched in 2024](<https://mmsp.gov.ma/fr/nos-metiers/connectivit%C3%A9>) for the areas 4G does not reach. The ministry reported that [PNHD 1 had covered 10,620 of the 10,740 localities targeted, 98.88 per cent, at the end of March 2024](<https://mmsp.gov.ma/fr/nos-metiers/connectivit%C3%A9>). The minister said the second phase [is carried out with the support of the Universal Telecommunications Service Fund](<https://www.lavieeco.com/au-royaume/plan-national-du-haut-debit-un-taux-de-realisation-de-99-pour-la-premiere-phase/>). In the last twelve months, on 16 November 2026, the minister told the House that [phase two provides for 2,000 rural zones](<https://en.le360.ma/technology/ai-rural-internet-access-and-public-services-ahmed-rahhou-unveils-moroccos-next-big-reforms_FA5XWVGDKRA7FAE2YUFSXCVX4E/>). No period beyond 2026 has been found for the second phase.

In 2024 the government told [ITU's ICT Regulatory Tracker](<https://app.gen5.digital/tracker/metrics>) that Madagascar has a national plan that involves broadband. The answer was self-reported. The entry names no plan and gives no title, adoption date, period or broadband targets. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No budget line, universal service fund allocation or financed programme tied to the plan has been found for the last three years. Operating would need money committed to the plan in the past three years: a budget line, a universal service fund allocation or a financed programme tied to it.

In a [2015 article](<http://bamada.net/connectivite-et-haut-debit-large-concertation-sur-la-mise-en-oeuvre-du-large-bande>) L'Essor reports that the regulator AMRTP held a launch workshop in Bamako for a study on the broadband implementation strategy. The study is to produce a short, medium and long-term broadband development plan, together with the introduction of 4G. The article does not report a plan adopted by the government or the minister. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source has been found that says a national broadband plan is adopted and still running, and nothing shows money committed to one. Establishing would need a national broadband plan adopted by the government or the minister, with its period not ended.

In December 2024 the government launched the Internet for All project, [according to the U.S. International Trade Administration](<https://www.trade.gov/market-intelligence/mozambique-digital-transformation-strategy>). It aims to raise internet access from under 25% of the population to 100% by 2030. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed: the [Wearetech.africa report of 23 July 2026](<https://www.wearetech.africa/fr/fils/actualites/telecom/mozambique-un-portail-national-du-haut-debit-pour-etendre-la-couverture-telecoms>) describes an Internet Para Todos programme running to 2030. Its targets are 80% mobile penetration, 95% territorial coverage and 99% network availability. No funding or delivery figures have been found, and no source says the plan is formally adopted. Establishing would need a national broadband plan adopted by the government or the minister, with its period not ended.

The ministry's final study of February 2019 [proposes a Stratégie Nationale Haut Débit / Plan National du Haut Débit for 2019-2025](<https://mtnima.gov.mr/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/strategie_promotion_hd_rim_volum-1_2.pdf>). It sets coverage of all Moughataas as the short-term aim and the whole country as the medium-term aim, and puts the investment at 623 million US dollars over 25 years, as an estimate. The study states no adoption by the government or a minister. The ministry's January 2019 action plan carries the name [Stratégie Nationale de Promotion du Haut Débit](<https://mtnima.gov.mr/sites/default/files/piecesjointes/strategie_promotion_hd_rim_volum-2.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a national broadband plan adopted by the government or the minister, with its period not ended.

The Ministry of Information and Communication Technology issued the [National Broadband Policy 2012-2020 (NBP2012)](<https://mitci.govmu.org/mitci/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/National-Broadband-Policy-2012-2020.pdf>) in January 2012. Its stated period ran from 2012 to 2020, and the document names no successor policy. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No other national broadband plan for Mauritius has been found from any year, including after 2020. Establishing would need a national broadband plan adopted by the government or the minister, with its period not ended.

Malawi's National Broadband Strategy ran from 2019 to 2023. [Ecofin Agency reported in October 2025](<https://www.ecofinagency.com/news-digital/0810-49382-malawi-launches-broadband-mapping-system-to-bridge-coverage-gaps>) that it aimed to raise broadband penetration from 4.5% to 35% and average speeds from 256 Kbps to 5 Mbps. The report names no plan that follows it. On 7 October 2025 the regulator MACRA launched a national broadband mapping system, meant to find and fill coverage gaps between 2025 and 2028. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source has been found that says a national broadband plan is adopted and still running. Establishing would need a national broadband plan adopted by the government or the minister, with its period not ended.

The Minister of Information and Communication Technology signed the [National Broadband Policy](<https://www.lac.org.na/laws/2020/7308.pdf>) on 27 July 2020. Government Gazette No. 7308 published it on 14 August 2020. In the last twelve months, [Cabinet approved a revised policy and implementation plan at its meetings of 13 and 27 October 2026](<https://neweralive.na/cabinet-briefs-15/>). It directed the ICT ministry to begin implementation. The National Digital Strategy, [reported in February 2026](<https://www.telecomreviewafrica.com/articles/features/28266-towards-a-5g-enabled-digitalized-namibia-in-2026/>), aims to raise internet use from 53% to 90% by 2030. No budget line or fund allocation tied to the plan has been found. Operating would need money committed to the plan.

Nigeria's National Broadband Plan 2020-2025 [expired at the end of December 2025](<https://guardian.ng/technology/broadband-nigeria-misses-2020-2025-target-mulls-new-2025-2030-plan/>). It aimed for 70 percent broadband penetration, and [NCC data put it at 51.97 percent in December 2025](<https://businessday.ng/pro/article/nigeria-expanded-broadband-but-missed-its-70-penetration-target/>). In the last twelve months, in April 2026, an NCC executive commissioner said the regulator was [drawing up a successor](<https://nairametrics.com/2026/04/30/telecom-operators-push-for-new-policy-as-nnbp-2020-2025-fails-expectations/>). [ThisDay put penetration at 58.22 percent in August 2026](<https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/05/with-58-22-broadband-penetration-nigeria-far-from-attaining-70-target/>). No successor has been found as adopted. Establishing would need a national broadband plan adopted by the government or the minister, with its period not ended.

The government [updated its National Broadband Policy and Strategy in 2022](<https://www.telecomreviewafrica.com/articles/reports-and-coverage/13149-rwandas-masterclass-in-digital-penetration-a-use-case-for-african-counterparts/>), Telecom Review Africa reported in October 2025. The update ended the commitment to a single wholesale network and introduced technology neutrality. The same report estimates 4G coverage reaching 100% by the end of 2025, with 3G at 99.71%, and sets neither figure against a target of the policy. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No budget line, universal service fund allocation or financed programme tied to the plan has been found for the last three years. Operating would need money committed to the plan in the past three years.

A [ministry slide deck of 2017](<https://www.itu.int/dms_pub/itu-d/oth/07/0d/D070D0000040001PDFE.pdf>) presents the guidelines of the Plan national haut/très haut débit, tied to Sénégal Numérique 2025. It sets out objectives, a diagnosis of the infrastructure and proposed investments. The deck does not state that the plan was adopted. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source has been found that says a national broadband plan is adopted and still running, and nothing shows money committed to one. Establishing would need a national broadband plan adopted by the government or the minister, with its period not ended.

Sierra Leone's Ministry of Communication, Technology and Innovation held a [validation workshop](<https://gleanersl.com/communications-ministry-poise-to-address-broadband-connectivity-challenges/>) on its National Broadband Strategy for 2023 to 2028 on 28 February 2024. [In January 2025 the minister said the government had passed it](<https://moice.gov.sl/minister-salima-outlines-accomplishments-in-the-tech-sector/>). ITEdgeNews [reported on 31 January 2025](<https://www.itedgenews.africa/sierra-leone-partners-with-starlink-to-expand-university-internet/>) that a government agreement to bring Starlink internet to 12 universities is in line with the strategy, and gave no cost. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No budget line, fund allocation or financed programme tied to the strategy has been found for the last three years. Operating would need money committed to the plan in the past three years.

The count rose from 1.3 million in 2024 to 1.9 million in 2025. The report does not give the rise as a figure against a target of the plan. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No budget line or fund allocation tied to the plan has been found. Operating would need money committed to the plan.

Chad's government launched Tchad Connexion 2030, which [TechAfrica News reported on 18 July 2025](<https://techafricanews.com/2025/07/18/chad-launches-1-5b-digital-strategy-to-connect-citizens-by-2030/>) as a national digital strategy running to 2030. Its targets are at least 80 percent national internet coverage and about 80 percent mobile penetration. [Ecofin, on 10 December 2025](<https://www.ecofinagency.com/news-digital/1012-51293-chad-finalizes-digital-law-to-align-national-framework-with-global-standards>), gives US$1.5bn of planned digital investment. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed: [Biometric Update, on 16 March 2026](<https://www.biometricupdate.com/202603/chad-uses-national-biometric-registry-to-boost-govt-systems-interoperability>), reports that the government is implementing it. No budget line or universal service fund allocation tied to the plan has been found for the last three years. Operating would need money committed to the plan.

The communication technologies ministry's fibre optic page names a national strategy for very high speed broadband, the Stratégie Nationale pour le Développement du très haut débit, which [dates from 2013](<https://www.mtc.gov.tn/index.php?id=296>). The page sits under the digital infrastructure axis of Tunisie Digitale 2020. It gives no period for the strategy, names nothing that replaces it, and states no budget and no figures against the strategy. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No budget line, universal service fund allocation or financed programme tied to the plan has been found for the last three years. Operating would need money committed to the plan in the past three years.

On 26 June 2026 Tanzania's Ministry of Communication and Information Technology [reported](https://www.mawasiliano.go.tz/news/kamati-ya-uongozi-ya-usimamizi-wa-mkakati-wa-taifa-wa-mawasiliano-ya-intaneti-ya-kasi-yafanya-kikao-cha-kwanza-dodoma) the first meeting of a Steering Committee that oversees the National High-Speed Internet Communication Strategy. A regulator's presentation of March 2026 lists the [Tanzania National Broadband Strategy 2021-2026](<https://www.itu.int/itu-d/sites/projectumc/wp-content/uploads/sites/42/2026/03/Tanzania-UMC-workshop.pdf>) among the country's digital policies. In the last twelve months the strategy was cited and not changed. The ministry report gives no period and says nothing of targets, funding or results. No budget line, universal service fund allocation or financed programme tied to the plan has been found for the last three years. Operating would need money committed to the plan in the past three years.

Uganda's [National Broadband Policy 2018](<https://www.itu.int/hub/publication/d-uga-natbrpo-2024/>) is the broadband plan under implementation, according to a review by the Ministry of ICT and National Guidance and the ITU published on 12 January 2026. The review lists, for each objective and strategy, the activities undertaken, the outcomes and the level of implementation reported by stakeholders. It gives no end date for the policy and names no replacement. In the last twelve months the policy was reviewed and not changed. No figures against the plan's targets have been found, and no budget line, universal service fund allocation or financed programme tied to it. Operating would need money committed to the plan in the past three years.

South Africa's broadband plan is [SA Connect, a policy of 2013](<https://www.gov.za/documents/notices/electronic-communications-act-international-mobile-telecommunications-roadmap-2>) that sets the aim of broadband for all. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed. In July 2026 the regulator ICASA named it as the existing national policy in its [draft IMT Roadmap 2026](<https://www.icasa.org.za/news/2026/icasa-publishes-draft-imt-roadmap-and-implementation-plans>). An [August 2026 article](<https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2026-08-03-sas-radio-spectrum-revolution-answers-mobile-network-operators-prayers/>) gives its target as universal access at an average of 100Mbps by 2030, with no figure for delivery. No budget line, universal service fund allocation or financed programme tied to the plan has been found for the last three years. Operating would need money committed to it.

The Ministry of Technology and Science's [National Digital Transformation Strategy 2023-2027](<https://www.mots.gov.zm/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/National-Digital-Transformation-Strategy.pdf>) sets broadband targets, including national broadband coverage of 80 percent and average broadband speed rising from 2.73 to 5.00 mbps. It also lists development of a national broadband master plan. In the last twelve months, in December 2025, the policy working group at the [Africa Broadband Maps national event](<https://africabbmaps.itu.int/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Africa-BB-Maps-Project-Zambia-National-Event-Report.pdf>) in Lusaka concluded that Zambia lacks a national broadband policy and recommended formulating one. No stand-alone broadband policy has been found. No budget line, universal service fund allocation or financed programme tied to the plan has been found for the last three years. Operating would need money committed to the plan.

Zimbabwe's ICT minister, Dr Tatenda Mavetera, said the government came up with a [National Broadband Plan](<https://www.heraldonline.co.zw/govt-develops-new-ict-policy/>), the Herald reported on 12 October 2023, and [launched the plan on 7 March 2024](<https://gemnation.co.zw/mavetera-launches-ict-policies/>) at Somabula. It covers 2020 to 2030. The Herald names the Ministry of ICT, Postal and Courier Services as its owner. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No budget line, universal service fund allocation or financed programme tied to the plan has been found for the last three years, and no figures against its own targets. Operating would need money committed to the plan in the past three years.
